answer: The cipher test I would run is Signed pension contribution history with fund attestation: contributions a pension fund logged for years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that contributions a pension fund logged for years — so privacy survives, and the orchard is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the cedar of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
